extension_points.name: Code extension API
extension_points.detail: product.json at Contents/Resources/app/product.json; per-user folder ~/.vscode; CLI Contents/Resources/app/bin/code takes --user-data-dir and --extensions-dir

extension_points.name: Accessibility (AX) API
extension_points.detail: every app; needs the Accessibility permission, reads and drives the UI

routes.name: settings and data files
routes.reason: cheapest, but reaches only what the app already reads; state: ~/Library/Application Support/Code, ~/Library/Preferences/com.microsoft.VSCode.plist

routes.name: Code extension API
routes.reason: the makers' extension point: can add UI and behaviour; product.json at Contents/Resources/app/product.json; per-user folder ~/.vscode; CLI Contents/Resources/app/bin/code takes --user-data-dir and --extensions-dir

routes.name: URL schemes
routes.reason: deep links (vscode://); trigger only. Caveat: `open` routes to an already-running instance, which may be the user's real profile

routes.name: Accessibility (AX) API
routes.reason: read and drive the UI; needs the Accessibility permission and acting through it is driving input, so ask first; the electron UI exposes a thin AX tree

routes.name: renderer script via DevTools Protocol
routes.reason: launch-time renderer script over the DevTools Protocol (--remote-debugging-port, lab profile, session only); app files untouched; check the app's terms first: a prohibition on client modification puts this out of scope

routes.name: network capture of the app's own traffic
routes.reason: your own account and data only; rarely needed for an app mod

routes.name: companion tool beside the app
routes.reason: rebuild the part you need next to the app, from its data files or API; most work, and the user sees it outside the app

routes.name: edit the app's files
routes.reason: editing a signed bundle breaks its seal: that defeats an integrity check; an updater would overwrite the edit anyway
